activity_context.topic_title: Symmetry Properties of the Standard Normal Distribution

feedback.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14069722/assets/8a6467813ccf982906fb5d1d8cd5c5c88b984c22a1e238715c65315a7772249c.png)

For a random variable $Z∼N(0,1),$ we have the following symmetry property for $a>0:$

$$
P(Z>a)=P(Z<-a)=Φ(-a)
$$

We're given that $Z∼N(0,1),$ and we wish to compute $P(Z<-0.38).$ The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14069722/assets/ee2aebec9953a09dca6eab5c7e5434240885a383a6701638fffdaa9ee9cfeb40.png)

By symmetry, this equals the area corresponding to the probability $P(Z>0.38).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14069722/assets/619fae52bde8b2da729095f733e1ea1411132fffe70cc23e252a83cbb2e7ff23.png)

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z<-0.38) & =P(Z>0.38) \\  & =1-P(Z<0.38) \\  & =1-Φ(0.38) \\  & =1-0.6480 \\  & =0.3520.\end{aligned}
$$
